That insight motivates an imitation method regulating alignment between latent variations and output actions. Hardware tests confirm a few seconds of demonstration suffice to train walking skills from scratch with robustness.
arxiv-2603-07261: Panja, Younes and Chakraborty build forecasters that turn chaotic time series into plain algebraic equations a reader can inspect. One tool adapts a neural equation-learning design to forecasting, while the other searches equation shapes by evolution. Both were tested on many chaotic attractors plus real dengue and sea-temperature series. They match strong baselines on short-range forecasts while showing their working in readable form.
arxiv-2603-07761: Zanieri and Kountouris derive entanglement fidelity math for standard quantum noise models, including depolarizing, dephasing, Pauli-X, Werner-Holevo, general Pauli and amplitude-damping channels. Entanglement fidelity measures how well a channel keeps links with a hidden reference. For each model they express fidelity through a general input density state via Schumacher's Kraus approach. That approach gives a recipe for any fully positive trace-keeping map with finite Kraus form. A two-letter tunable alphabet source makes entanglement keeping depend on channel and source settings, enabling contrasts and rankings.
arxiv-2603-07861: Shelby gives a practitioner guide to the United Kingdom Cyber Security and Resilience Bill, brought to Parliament in late 2025 as the biggest cyber law reform in near a decade. He maps its wider scope: managed service firms, data centres and key suppliers. It sets one-day and three-day incident report clocks, with fines that can reach 17 million pounds or a share of world sales. He sets the bill beside European rules and shows how zero-trust design and a national assessment frame can ground compliance plans.
arxiv-2603-08161: Cretton and colleagues match dislocation patterning models against live images for the first time. With live Dark-Field X-ray Microscopy (DFXM), they map orientations in pure aluminium deformed along [100]. They spot dislocation boundaries on {111} slip planes, appearing before any usual cell structure. Nickel stands in as the FCC analogue in a continuum dislocation dynamics (CDD) simulation, chosen for its high stacking fault energy (SFE). Its DFXM images predict the boundary types, showing experiment and model can sharpen ideas about plastic flow despite gaps in strain rates and length scales.
arxiv-2603-08261: Gostelow and colleagues run magnetoconvection simulations in a spherical shell to track equatorial symmetry during the transition from weak to strong-field dynamos. At moderate convective driving, dynamo simulations often split into two broad dipolar regimes, sorted by magnetic field strength or by dominant force balance. These regimes can blend smoothly into one another but can also be bistable, especially at low diffusivity. Since geodynamo runs cannot use realistic parameters, the authors track the strong-field branch, the one for Earth's core, as a special limit.
arxiv-2603-08461: Burgholzer and colleagues track SH generation in thermally oxidized molybdenum disulfide flakes, from one to seven layers. Oxidation shifts the SH response a lot in every structure studied. Tests at varied power show it advancing over up to six hours in these conditions. Varying light polarization reveals structural changes, while the depth stays in the top layer and the effect differs by layer count. Band structure theory backs the findings: thermal oxidation progress can be watched with non-resonant, non-invasive SH microscopy through distinct signs in the nonlinear response.
arxiv-2603-08661: Jordi Muñoz Vicente rebuilds a 3D Gaussian splatting pipeline in low-level C++ and CUDA code. Moving off high-level Python cuts host-device sync and training delay, with new kernels for splitting, edge scoring, and scale scheduling. On the Mip-NeRF360 set, a lean variant trains faster with fewer Gaussians at better quality, and the full variant lifts PSNR over the ADC baseline.
arxiv-2603-09061: Changhu Wang and colleagues screen place-linked genes in spatial gene maps with no model assumed. Huge data makes finding genes tied to unknown spatial clusters a central task. Their MM-test, a quasi-likelihood score paired with a knockoff step, controls the false discovery share, beats existing methods across lab tests and 34 data sets, and maps 3D brain structures.
arxiv-2603-09361: Saima Bashir and colleagues study how phonons reshape qubit dynamics in the Jaynes-Cummings model, where strong qubit-phonon coupling yields the Jaynes-Cummings-Holstein model. Under anti-adiabatic conditions they use a unitary transformation and a Redfield-type non-Markovian master equation to get a tractable problem. Their formula for time-dependent coherence includes both cavity loss and phonon dressing. They find phonon coupling suppresses non-Markovian behavior by weakening the effective qubit-cavity link, while polaronic dressing mutes detuning effects.
arxiv-2603-10261: Ihor Kendiukhov reports extracting a compact blood-cell algorithm from the single-cell model scGPT, described as the first useful extraction of its kind. He finds a small internal map of blood development, checked on an outside cell panel and by transfer to a separate donor panel. The three-step method exports frozen attention weights, adds a light adaptor, and fits a task readout without retraining on target data. The extracted algorithm leads rival tools on ordering and subtype tasks, and stays strong when cut to one attention head.
arxiv-2603-10661: Ryma Boumazouza and co-authors propose FAME, a method for formal, abstract, and minimal explanations of neural networks, grounded in abstract interpretation. It is the first such method to scale to large networks while shrinking explanation size. Dedicated perturbation domains remove any need for traversal order, and the domains shrink as LiRPA bounds discard irrelevant features. The authors also give a way to measure how far an abstract minimal explanation sits from a true one. Against VERIX+, FAME gained on both size and runtime.
arxiv-2603-10761: Dario Benedetti, Ilya Chevyrev, and Razvan Gurau give two new proofs that path integral and stochastic quantizations of scalar Euclidean quantum field theories agree. Both proofs use Taylor interpolations indexed by forests, in the style of constructive field theory. The first works term by term in the Feynman expansion, where forests appear as spanning subgraphs of Feynman diagrams. The second works at the level of the whole path integral and avoids expanding the full perturbation series. Together they offer a pedestrian route between the two quantization schemes.
arxiv-2603-10961: Prithviraj Tarale and coauthors give wearable accelerometer learning a biological twist. They tokenize wrist motion the way motor control theory says movement is built. It is built from elementary units called submovements. Their token is a movement segment, a finite run of submovements. A transformer encoder is pretrained by masked reconstruction of these tokens. The corpus is a large national survey corpus. The learned representations beat strong self-supervised baselines. They do so across six activity-recognition benchmarks with disjoint subjects. Focus shifts from raw waveform shape to movement structure.
arxiv-2603-11061: Van Le and Tan Le build a hybrid quantum-classical encoding to predict residue-level pKa values. Such values sit at the heart of protein function, stability, and reactivity. Classical descriptors often generalize poorly across varied biochemical settings. So they add a Gaussian kernel-based quantum-inspired feature map and merge its output with normalized structural inputs. A deep quantum neural network reads the merged encoding. It does better than classical baselines across contexts. It also holds up on an experimental benchmark and an amyloid-beta case study.
arxiv-2603-11361: Ross Turner and Georgia Stewart propose that remnant radio lobes in massive clusters vanish quickly once their jets switch off. Lobes held up mainly by jet momentum implode. Analyzing the asymptotics of a dynamical model against full simulations, they find one result. Weak-jet remnants in massive clusters are unstable to implosion within a few million years at most. Such remnants would be undercounted by at least a factor of five beside poorer groups. Surveys may badly underestimate the feedback low-powered jets deliver near cluster cores.
arxiv-2603-11561: Brain and co-authors ask how fast a Mars-like planet would lose its air around Barnard's star, an old M dwarf, at Mars-like flux. Escape runs through thermal, ion, and photochemical routes, plus sputtering. The team sets the planet at a distance with the same total stellar flux Mars gets today. Thermal escape dominates, at rates two to five orders of magnitude above present-day Mars. Such a planet, they conclude, would hold no real atmosphere past tens of millions of years.
arxiv-2603-12061: Karamitros, McKelvey, Panghal, and Pilaftsis define a class of critical unstable qubits in particle physics. They track two-level systems with Bloch vectors for energy levels and decay widths. The critical case sets those two vectors at right angles, with a size ratio below one. In a co-decaying frame such systems show unusual coherence and decoherence oscillations. Fourier tools yield new observables that gauge how far the swings stray from a sine shape. Neutral meson systems supply limits and a summary table.
arxiv-2603-12261: Pach, Bader, Bouniot, Belongie, and Akata uncover a latent color subspace inside a top image generator. Fine color control stays hard because semantic coding in these models is poorly understood. Inside the FLUX.1 VAE latent space, they find a structure that mirrors hue, saturation, and lightness. That reading both predicts and directly controls color in generated images. Their control method needs no training and works by closed-form moves in latent space. Code for the approach is public for others to test and extend.
arxiv-2603-12861: Myriam Benisty and co-authors map vertical gas flows in 14 protoplanetary disks for the exoALMA program. Such flows, from winds to meridional circulation, shape the first stages of planet growth. They model the Keplerian field and read velocity residuals in two CO lines. Most disks show vertical motion of a few tens of meters per second. Some show wind bases, and two show fast spiral flows. Deep line data thus reveal vertical motion as a common disk trait.
arxiv-2603-12961: Cristina-Andreea Alexe summarizes recent electroweak measurements from the CMS experiment at the Large Hadron Collider. The standard model was tested through precise values of its key electroweak parameters. Proton-proton collisions reached record center-of-mass energies in these studies. Many results were firsts, or the best yet at a proton collider, some rivaling lepton collider precision. Topics span W and Z production cross sections and the forward-backward asymmetry in Drell-Yan events. Tau lepton traits, multiboson output, and vector boson scattering are covered too.
arxiv-2603-14061: Schvöllner and Pastine study induced paths and cycles in factor graphs built from split graphs. The factor graph encodes how 2-switch moves reshape the split graph. Induced paths force chains of neighborhood inclusions among their vertices. Degrees along such a path then change in a monotone way. As a result, induced cycles can have length at most four. Only the first or last edge of an induced path can be simple, which bounds the graph's diameter.
arxiv-2603-14261: Alaoui, Halloumi, and Viglialoro study a two-dimensional Keller-Segel chemotaxis model with a Gompertz growth term. The classic model can blow up as cells pile together. Logistic growth with quadratic decay tames that pile-up, and weaker damping has also been shown to work. Gompertz growth damps still more weakly than the terms used before. The authors find conditions under which solutions exist for all time and stay bounded. The work maps how much growth control this system needs.
arxiv-2603-14361: Pereira, Fernandes, and Barros build BROTHER, a system that spots ambivalence and hesitancy in natural video. These states show as faint, mixed signals across face, voice, and words, not as plain expressions. Their pipeline fuses features from all three modes, with a text mode built to catch timing shifts in speech. Fifteen mode mixes are tried across three classifier types, and the best-calibrated models are kept. A particle swarm vote then blends them, with a penalty that drops overfit members.
arxiv-2603-14461: Mallick and co-authors present CATFA-Net, a network for medical image segmentation. Standard convolutional blocks miss long-range links between image regions. Transformer models capture global context but cost more and can lack stability. CATFA-Net pairs a hybrid transformer encoder with a light convolutional decoder. A new Context Addition Attention block tracks links across images without quadratic cost. Features from both branches merge before the decoder runs. The authors report sharp masks with lower cost and faster inference than prior designs.
arxiv-2603-14561: Li and Wu fix variance estimates for semiparametric estimators with second-order remainders. Standard practice trusts the influence-function variance from a von Mises expansion. That trust fails when the remainder adds real variance of its own. Sandwich errors then run small, and Wald intervals miss too often. The authors split total variance into influence and remainder parts. They show when the sandwich can fail and prove fixes work. Leave-one-out jackknife and cluster bootstrap both track total variance under stated conditions.
arxiv-2603-14661: Barker and co-authors judge what open-source 5G platforms can credibly measure with AtlasRAN. Testbeds range from simulators to radio hardware loops and digital twins. Like interfaces can hide unlike timing and buffering behavior. AtlasRAN pairs claim paths with an execution-regime matrix to grade platforms. A case study contrasts OpenAirInterface RFSim with the Sionna Research Kit. Uplink goodput falls from about 114 to 35 megabits per second as users grow from one to six. Timing fidelity, not feature match, sets the verdict.
arxiv-2603-14761: Tang probes a commonsense gap in large language models with BrainBench, a set of 100 brainteasers. Twenty categories each target one failure mode. Traps span hidden physical limits, scope tricks and hijacked default assumptions. Eight frontier models face the set, four Claude and four GPT. Each question runs ten times under a zero-shot protocol. The best model reaches only 80.3% accuracy. The worst, GPT-4o, scores 39.7%. Accuracy-consistency gaps of 6 to 16 points expose shaky reasoning, Tang reports.
arxiv-2603-15161: Knobloch and co-authors study localized space-time patterns in the Purwins model, a three-variable FitzHugh-Nagumo system. The patterns grow from a subcritical finite-wavenumber Hopf instability. Numerical continuation traces snaking branches of standing and traveling waves on a line. Weakly nonlinear theory backs the computations. The results explain so-called jumping oscillons and an unusual homoclinic snaking of traveling pulses. On disks, they find spots that hug the wall, travel along it, or jump. One-dimensional results help read the two-dimensional ones.
arxiv-2603-15861: Gladyshev and co-authors trap light sideways with the transverse Kerker effect. Dielectric particles can scatter light mostly across the beam path. Full forward cancelation from one object breaks the optical theorem. A single photonic mode still hits the ideal sideways pattern. In metasurface arrays, the mode turns into a bound state in the continuum. Quality factors tune freely with no symmetry breaking needed. Lab tests in visible light confirm the concept. The states stay sharp across a wide momentum range.
arxiv-2603-16361: Apergis and co-authors test the Marana CMOS camera on the sky at the NGTS facility in Chile. The camera rode on one telescope while a CCD camera watched from a neighbor. Both observed transits around eight bright exoplanet host stars. The CMOS matched the CCD's precision, near 500 ppm at 30 minutes. Its faster readout caught 20% more photons per unit time. The team judges modern CMOS cameras well suited to time-series photometry.
arxiv-2603-16561: Dey and co-authors seek one origin for the many neutrino mass matrix textures. Phenomenology uses diverse texture patterns, each added by hand. Their framework rests on the Δ(27) symmetry group. A Type-I plus Type-II seesaw supplies the masses. Vacuum alignments, model parameters, and Yukawa choices interact inside it. That interplay reproduces several known textures with no extra assumptions. A single minimal frame thus unifies the viable patterns.
arxiv-2603-17161: Cai, Sun, and Lu present GazeOnce360, a model that estimates the gaze of many people from one upward facing fisheye camera. Standard gaze systems use forward facing cameras with narrow views. Their setting covers a full 360 degree scene around a tabletop camera. They built MPSGaze360, a large synthetic dataset rendered in Unreal Engine with 3D gaze and eye landmark labels. The model uses rotational convolutions to handle fisheye distortion. A dual resolution design fuses global context with high resolution eye regions.
arxiv-2603-17261: Zhang and co-authors present NTSSL, a method that links Bitcoin transactions to network users by watching traffic. Bitcoin addresses carry no real world names, yet network layer attacks can erode that privacy. Prior methods often suffer from low precision. NTSSL joins network traffic analysis with semi supervised learning, using unsupervised methods to mint pseudo labels at low cost. A variant, NTSSL+, adds transaction clustering results in a cross layer analysis. In experiments, the method performed 1.6 times better than the existing machine learning approach.
arxiv-2603-17361: Goyal and co-authors tackle citation recommendation for new papers in the wild. Their Profiler module captures how humans cite, without training and without bias toward some sources. It improves the pool of candidate papers at low cost. They also add an inductive test setting with strict time rules, closer to real use. A reranker named DAVINCI then sets new best scores on several benchmarks, they report.
arxiv-2603-17461: He and co-authors present AR-CoPO, a training method for streaming autoregressive video generators. Standard reinforcement methods struggle with short, low-noise sampler paths. AR-CoPO forks a video at one random chunk and builds neighbor candidates there. Sequence-level rewards then drive a local policy update at that fork. A replay buffer of reference clips adds stable examples. Gains held both in-domain and out-of-domain, they report.
arxiv-2603-17561: Menichella compiles a mass inventory of the Solar System without the Sun. He draws on spacecraft data, orbit fits, and surveys of asteroids and trans-Neptunian objects. A Monte Carlo run with 100,000 draws gives a median total of 462 Earth masses. The giant planets hold 96.2 percent of that mass. Nearly all the error comes from the inner Oort cloud, he finds. Rubin Observatory data may shrink that gap.
arxiv-2603-17661: Adroja and Amrutiya study finite and semi-finite vector bundles on complex tori. They give an explicit split of such bundles into torsion and unipotent parts. That split drives the main structural result of the study. The extended Nori fundamental group scheme of a complex torus then factors as a product. One factor is its etale part and the other its unipotent part, they prove. The result ties bundle types to group scheme shape.
arxiv-2603-17861: Chazottes, Collet, and Redig build a transport-entropy frame for Gaussian concentration on infinite lattices. Sensitivity is scored by the l2 norm of local oscillations across the product space. No metric on configurations can induce their transport costs, they show. In finite volume, their probability metric and coupling functional turn out to be the same object. That equality extends Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality past metric settings. Marton's coupling bound then equals Gaussian concentration in all volumes.
arxiv-2603-17961: Anslow, Landeau, Bonsor, Itcovitz, and Shorttle find a paradox in Earth's late veneer story. Mantle rocks hold extra highly siderophile elements, blamed on late impacts after the giant impact phase. Metal from impactors over one kilometer should sink straight to the core, they show. Small impactors then must carry the whole signal, which demands an implausible total mass. Large cores must somehow shred into fine bits, or the veneer was rich in oxidized rock.
arxiv-2603-18061: Burton uses SIREN network error as a diagnostic for regularity loss in Navier-Stokes flow. SIRENs have smooth sine activations, so they cannot fit non-smooth features. Spectral theory ties their error to local Sobolev regularity of the field. He splits the field into an analytic base and a learned pressure residual. On the Taylor-Green vortex, error focus grew from 4.9 to 13.6 times as viscosity fell, near the stagnation point.
arxiv-2603-18161: Abdulhai and co-authors show that LLMs distort written language in voice, tone, and meaning. A user study found heavy LLM use raised neutral, off-stance essays by nearly 70%. Heavy users also said the text felt less creative and less in their own voice. Even grammar-only edits to 2021 essays shifted semantic meaning in clear ways. LLM peer reviews at a top AI conference also scored work a full point higher.
arxiv-2603-18461: Nishimura and co-authors present a cell-type prototype-informed network that estimates gene expression from pathology images. Bulk expression sums over many cells, but past models ignore that cell-level origin. Public single-cell data yield cell-type prototypes that capture stable co-variation patterns. The network learns cell-type weights from images and maps prototypes to observed expression. It tops Spearman correlation on six datasets and shows which cell types drive each call.
arxiv-2603-18961: Barrera and co-authors prove a smoothness result for a p-adic family space. They assume a non-abelian form of the Leopoldt conjecture. Under that claim, the space lies flat over weight space at key classical points. They then apply the result to a special automorphic form whose local part is Steinberg. With a tangent condition, two kinds of L-invariants match. This also backs a claim that such invariants do not depend on the degree choice.
arxiv-2603-19261: Nouri offers a new rule for how tokenizers merge letter pairs when they split text. Standard BPE merges the pairs seen most often, which can reward mere bulk over true cohesion. The new rule scores pairs with a z-statistic against an independence baseline. A gain term keeps an eye on compression at the same time. On WikiText-103 slices, a small model shows 13 percent lower perplexity. Bits per character also improve by about one percent. Most size tests favor the new rule.
arxiv-2603-19361: Saccani and co-authors boost the performance of constrained nonlinear control while keeping safety firm. A predictive safety filter acts as the base controller and enforces all limits. A second controller proposes stronger inputs for that filter to screen. It also sends a signal that tunes how fast the filter's Lyapunov bound must fall. Any controller of this form keeps the loop stable and safe, they prove. The design also widens the set of safe paths beyond standard filters. A swinging pendulum with a moving obstacle shows the gain.
arxiv-2603-19461: Zhang and co-authors build agents that can rewrite the very code that improves them. Prior self-improving systems rely on fixed, hand-made meta rules. Their hyperagents fuse a task agent and a meta agent into one editable program. Even the edit procedure itself can be edited by the system. They extend the Darwin Gödel Machine to drop its coding-only tie. Across varied domains, the system improves over time with use. It beats baselines with no self-improvement and prior open-ended designs.
arxiv-2603-19961: Ousalah and co-authors estimate an object's full 6D pose from one RGB image, directly. Direct methods are fast but often less accurate than keypoint methods. They also tend to pool features globally, losing spatial detail, and use pose codes with jumps. Cov2Pose instead pools feature maps into a covariance matrix, a symmetric positive definite object. The pose is coded through a Cholesky factor of such a matrix. A manifold aware head then regresses the pose end to end. Tests, including partial occlusion, favor the new design.
arxiv-2603-20161: Cao and co-authors measure uncertainty in language model output by clustering tokens with like meanings. Most uncertainty methods resample many times or call helper models, which costs a lot. Semantic Token Clustering needs just one generation pass. It groups tokens by embedding similarity and shared prefixes. Uncertainty is then scored from the total probability mass of each meaning cluster. No auxiliary model is involved at any point. Results matched leading baselines on their tests. Compute overhead fell sharply compared with sampling-based rivals.
arxiv-2603-20461: Pattichis and co-authors study how to invert neural networks, finding inputs behind chosen outputs. Such inputs should reveal features the network links with each class. Their forward pass method uses root-finding with the input Jacobian. Their backward pass method inverts layer by layer from the top. Random null-space vectors add variety during the inversion steps. Tests cover transformer models and plain sequential networks. The methods produce random-like images that score near perfect classification. This exposes real weaknesses in the underlying networks.
arxiv-2603-20661: Wang and co-authors propose WWW.Serve, a shared network that links LLM services across the globe without a central boss. Central hosting hits scale limits while spare GPUs sit idle in many places. Past shared systems missed that providers compete with each other. They also forced one fixed stack and full task loads. WWW.Serve lets each provider set its own terms and pledge what it wants. Requests find their own path through the network. In tests, service goals met rose up to 1.5 times, and latency fell by 27.6 percent.
arxiv-2603-20761: Girotti and co-authors build the asymptotic statistical theory of irreducible quantum Markov chains. They ask which parameters of the dynamics can be identified from output. The identifiable set forms a stratified space called an orbifold. It comes from dividing the dynamics by state preserving symmetries. They link periodicity to the strata of this space. A quantum Fisher information rate is given in geometric terms. The output model then splits into Gaussian shift parts. These results ground optimal estimators for the dynamics.
arxiv-2603-20961: Costa and co-authors advance Graham's conjecture on ordering sets in abelian groups. The conjecture says a set of nonzero elements can be ordered so that all partial sums are distinct. It was lately proved for large primes, but stays open for general groups. With a recursive method, they prove any subset of size at most twenty is sequenceable. The bound rises to twenty two for zero-sum subsets. For a related conjecture, zero-sum subsets without inverse pairs are sequenceable up to size twenty three.
arxiv-2603-21061: Zhang and co-authors present LRHPerception, a real-time perception package for self-driving that uses one camera. Camera based driving work often favors accuracy over compute cost. Their system turns single view video into a five channel tensor with color, road segmentation, and pixel level depth. It adds object detection and trajectory prediction in the same frame. It runs at twenty nine frames per second on one GPU, a fivefold plus speedup over the fastest mapping based rival.
arxiv-2603-21461: Wedgwood and co-authors align language models with human preferences without retraining the model weights. Their DSPA method steers sparse autoencoder features at inference time, guided by a map built from preference triples. The map links prompt features to features that control generation, and only active features are adjusted. Across Gemma and Qwen models, DSPA improved chat scores while keeping multiple-choice accuracy. It stayed strong with little preference data and used far less compute than a two-stage rival.
arxiv-2603-21661: Zhao and co-authors teach rain removal models to face new scenes with no paired rainy photos from those scenes. Models trained on fake rain often fail on real weather. Their method needs only clear background images from the target place. A superpixel step pulls stable structure from the source data. A fusion step aligns that structure with target backgrounds by texture match, making varied fake rainy data. Multi-stage noise then fakes real rain streaks. Added to existing derainers, it lifted scores on unseen scenes by large margins.
arxiv-2603-21861: Bert and co-authors test whether energy loss in small collision systems can explain a flow signal. Their QCD model follows partons through a fluid medium, with size fixes for small systems. Tuned on large systems, it matches suppression data, even for neon and oxygen runs. Yet at high momentum it predicts almost no elliptic flow in any small system. They argue this is generic: such models decorrelate the hard and soft event planes, so the usual method reads v2 as near zero. That challenges flow readings in small systems.
arxiv-2603-22061: Petrov tests a design choice in abliteration, a method that strips refusal behavior from language models. Abliteration finds refusal directions in the model's activation space. Petrov asks whether a baseline matched by topic gives better directions. He tests this on the Qwen 3.5 2B model with matched prompt pairs. He finds topic-matched contrast yields no working refusal directions at any layer or weight. Unmatched contrast, on the same setup, removes refusal fully on six layers. His analysis shows matched subtraction cancels the shared activation signal.
arxiv-2603-22161: Kumaran and co-authors ask whether language models use their own confidence to steer behavior. Confidence can be read from outputs, but use is a separate question. The team designs a four-phase test around one choice: answer or abstain. Models apply an internal threshold on confidence when they decide to abstain. Steering experiments then give causal proof. Raising the confidence signal lowers abstention, and suppressing it raises abstention. Verbal confidence also predicts abstention, beyond the log-probability signal. The authors read this as structured metacognitive control.
arxiv-2603-22361: Ntelis and Said work out the dynamics of two dark energy models with pen-and-paper math. The models are phiCDM, with a rolling scalar field, and polyΛCDM, a modified gravity frame. They derive how the energy density ratios evolve in each model. Both are checked against the standard LCDM model and against numeric runs. The phiCDM math tracks LCDM within a fraction of a percent. The poly model shows a richer path through cosmic epochs. It ends at a cosmological constant attractor in the far future.
arxiv-2603-22461: Morras and co-authors revisit what neutron star and black hole mergers look like as a population. They reanalyze all such events in the latest gravitational-wave catalog with a waveform that captures orbital eccentricity and spin precession. The two double neutron star events look fully circular. One merger stands out with real eccentricity, hinting at a dynamical origin. The rest fit quiet binaries formed in isolation. The team then draws the first joint limits on mass, spin, and eccentricity for this class.
arxiv-2603-22561: Anthony asks whether a small neural network can split its work between intuition and deliberation. He tests the idea on a classic set of 64 syllogism problems with human answer patterns as the target. A plain network first learns to predict the full spread of human replies. A second design gives intuition and deliberation separate pathways, guided by mental-model theory. Deliberation tracks human answers better than intuition across test folds. Its inner states also settle into a sparse, varied pattern, hinting at reasoning-like structure.
arxiv-2603-22761: Lai and co-authors propose a new way to charge a quantum battery. Their protocol uses cyclic indefinite causal order across N chargers. Charging sequences are superposed rather than run in a fixed order. The authors observe bursts of charging efficiency under this scheme. The bursts last longer as N grows. They give a circuit model for the two-charger case. Proof-of-concept runs on IonQ, Quantinuum, and IBM quantum hardware confirm the bursts. The results match their theory and simulations.
arxiv-2603-23161: Ji and co-authors present a dual contrastive network for few-shot remote sensing scene classification. Few labeled samples make the task hard. Classes look alike, while one class can vary a lot. Their transfer-based network adds two contrastive branches in training. A context branch sharpens differences between classes. A detail branch stresses stable local features within a class. Each branch has its own feature network feeding the contrastive loss. Tests on four public remote sensing datasets show competitive results.
arxiv-2603-23361: Ota presents CDT-III, a model that follows biology's central dogma across DNA, RNA, and protein. Its Virtual Cell Embedder splits work by cell compartment. One stage models transcription in the nucleus, the other translation in the cytosol. On five genes, it scores r of 0.843 for RNA and 0.969 for protein. Adding the protein task sharpens RNA scores and DNA-level readouts. It also exposes a catch: most mRNA shifts come with opposite protein shifts. In a drug test, it predicted all 29 protein changes right.
arxiv-2603-23461: Mhammedi, Rakhlin, and Okolo give an efficient learner for a clean class of Markov decision processes. In these MDPs, the Bellman backup of any linear value function stays linear. Past efficient methods shrank the action space or leaned on strong oracles. Their setting uses deterministic transitions with random starts and rewards. For finite actions, the algorithm runs end to end with polynomial cost. For huge action spaces, it needs only a standard argmax oracle. It learns a near-optimal policy with cost polynomial in horizon and feature size.
arxiv-2603-23661: Leonhard, Lambertenghi, and Stocco present PerturbationDrive, a test rig for driver assistance systems. Neural driving stacks work in fair weather yet wobble under odd inputs. The framework packs over 30 image tweaks that mimic weather, light, and sensor flaws. Fresh variants shift over time or follow the model's own gaze. Tests run offline on stored sets or live in simulators. Road generation and search tools widen the scene mix further. The setup makes robustness checks repeatable across labs.
arxiv-2603-23761: Rickert and co-authors apply a new aperiodic defect model to a charged vacancy in phosphorene. Normal supercell methods can create false defect interactions and need charge fixes. The new model treats one defect inside the true crystal field and cuts the work to a fragment. This allows high-level molecular methods. They report a formation energy of 0.81 eV for the charged monovacancy, and an excitation energy of 1.95 eV. They present the model as a path to accurate defect studies in solids.
arxiv-2603-23961: Zhou and co-authors infer the stage of deep-sea cold seeps from microbial data with very few samples. Manned submersible surveys are costly and risky. Microbes offer a cheaper signal, but the dataset has only 13 samples against 26 features. Their model, GRMLR, adds an ecological knowledge graph as a structural prior. Graph penalties keep the logistic model in line with known ecology. At test time it needs only microbial profiles. It beats standard baselines by a clear margin, they report.
arxiv-2603-24061: Shinohara derives the conserved quantity and ensemble measure for MTK barostats with limited cell motion. Barostats control pressure in molecular simulations by letting the cell shape change. In the standard MTK form, all cell degrees of freedom are active. Shinohara restricts motion to a subset of cell axes. The conserved energy-like quantity keeps the same form, with the count of active axes in place of the full count. He verifies exact conservation and gives a full integration scheme. The dynamics sample the right ensemble on the restricted shapes.
arxiv-2603-24261: Liu and co-authors report that manganese substitution changes the magnetism of the chromium telluride Cr5Te8. They grow single crystals of the pure compound and of Cr4MnTe8. Manganese lifts the ordering temperature from 226 to 249 kelvin. It also raises the saturation moment per ion from 2.00 to 2.66 Bohr magnetons at 5 kelvin. That gain beats what manganese ions alone would add, so the swap also relieves spin compensation in the host. Calculations show a ferrimagnetic to ferromagnetic switch, driven by manganese in the van der Waals gaps.
arxiv-2603-24461: Tan and co-authors design a miniature fibre-reinforced soft bending actuator for robots that work inside the body. The single-chamber device is centimetre scale, with embedded Kevlar fibre to maximise bending while keeping a tight seal. A multi-stage casting process in silicones of varied stiffness builds it. The team tests helix winding patterns, fibre pitch, and fibre density against a detailed finite element model. The best design bends past 200 degrees in tests and stays robust up to 100 kilopascals, with radial expansion well restrained.
arxiv-2603-24561: Cohen and co-authors study X-ray superorbital modulation in the supergiant high-mass binary 4U 1538-52. Long-term Swift monitoring found the modulation, and several missions tracked a slow pulse period evolution that seems unrelated to flux changes. The team builds dynamic power spectra and intensity profiles from Swift and MAXI monitoring data. NuSTAR and NICER data probe pulsation and spectra across phases. The MAXI light curves confirm the modulation period seen by Swift, while pulse profiles and spectral parameters show no significant change across phases.
arxiv-2603-24761: Kerur and co-authors present eAID, an elastic scheme for dispersing erasure-coded data in distributed systems. Classic dispersal waits for responses from all but the worst-case number of faulty nodes, wasting healthy nodes' storage. eAID first estimates the actual number of faulty nodes, so dispersal completes fast when failures are few. After dispersal, it keeps listening for late responses. As more nodes reply, it prunes the fragments they store. An agile encoding varies the fragment count while keeping fragment size and reconstruction properties fixed, enabling this elasticity.
arxiv-2603-25361: Rupflin and Woodward bound how far near-perfect maps sit from odd, spiky minimizers of a classic energy. For degree-one maps from a closed surface to a sphere, the best energy is never quite reached. The true minimizer is a flat map plus one point of endless concentration. They ask if the energy gap controls the gap to that set. A new flow method reshapes the surface and the map in step. Sharp bounds follow for the spike's scale, and for distances near and far from it.
arxiv-2603-25561: Nair and D'Souza pair a genome-scale yeast model with machine learning to boost single-cell protein output. The Yeast9 model maps over four thousand reactions in the yeast cell. Flux balance runs over two thousand sampled profiles feed two regressors, which predict biomass near perfectly. A latent map finds four metabolic clusters. Twenty key reactions stand out, mostly in energy and amino-acid paths, and most prove essential in knockout tests. Guided tuning lifts biomass flux twelvefold. One generative arm failed its feasibility check, and they report that openly.
arxiv-2603-25761: Beyene and Dancy survey how OCR systems are evaluated, and what those tests leave out. Modern vision models now read documents, yet benchmarks center on modern Western institutional files. Historical archives rarely appear in training data or test sets. The authors review papers and datasets from 2006 to 2025 with the PRISMA method. They focus on Black historical newspapers as a key case. Most tests stress character accuracy on clean modern layouts. They miss column collapse, type errors, and invented text. The authors tie these gaps to structural invisibility and harm.
arxiv-2603-26261: Alkhatib and Tay extend conformal prediction to contrastive learning. Contrastive methods pull matched samples close and push unmatched ones apart in feature space. The authors build covering sets with learnable ball-like shapes that promise a chosen coverage rate for matched samples. At the same time, the sets aim to shut out as many unmatched samples as they can. Tests on fake and real image data show better trade-offs than plain distance-based conformal sets.
arxiv-2603-26661: von Lützow, Rössle, Schmid, and Nießner present GaussianGPT, a transformer that builds 3D scenes one token at a time. Most 3D generators use diffusion or flow matching, which refine a whole scene at once. Their model instead predicts 3D Gaussians directly in sequence. A sparse 3D autoencoder first packs Gaussian primitives into a discrete latent grid. A causal transformer with 3D rotary positions then writes the tokens in order. The step-by-step form supports scene completion, outpainting, and flexible generation lengths.
arxiv-2603-26861: Kumar and Yadav constrain a new one-parameter model of dark energy against recent cosmic data. The model's fluid departs from the standard cosmological constant picture. They fit it with Hubble data, the Pantheon+SH0ES supernova set, and DESI BAO DR2 measurements. The joint fit gives the new parameter as 0.239 plus or minus 0.07. That nonzero value hints at a departure from a pure constant. The model also shows a past shift from slowing expansion to the current speeding phase.
arxiv-2603-26961: Chester and Pandey build a gauge-covariant Hamilton picture for two teleparallel versions of general relativity. The theories are the metric and symmetric teleparallel equivalents. Torsion and nonmetricity play the role of velocities. Their conjugate momenta scale with the matching superpotentials. The actions give regular Legendre maps on the field-strength fibers. For both theories, the second Hamilton equation returns the Einstein field equations. In the ADM sector, the surface terms keep the standard deformation algebra.
arxiv-2603-27261: Fang proposes MD-RWKV-UNet for segmenting many organs in one medical scan. Organs vary widely in size and shape, and small ones are easily lost. The core block mixes deformable spatial shifts with a weighted key-value attention mechanism. Its receptive field adapts to local structural cues. Selective kernel attention chooses among convolution kernels of different sizes. A cross-stage fusion strategy blends features across encoder levels with dual attention. Experiments on Synapse and ACDC reached state-of-the-art results, notably on small organs.
arxiv-2603-27361: Candan and Servadio estimate a tumbling target's inertia tensor online with an augmented Kalman filter. Servicing and debris removal need precise tracking of uncooperative, spinning targets. Standard tools assume the target's mass traits are already known. Their filter tracks six-degree-of-freedom pose and the full inertia tensor jointly. Monocular CNN vision and LiDAR depth feed the coupled dynamics model. Adaptive noise keeps those estimates stable without freezing them. Monte Carlo runs show states and inertia values meeting together.
arxiv-2603-27761: Markov and co-authors clean quantum gate signals by predistorting them. Analog hardware warps the tones that drive entangling gates. Their team targets an acousto-optic modulator in a trapped-ion system. The ion species is strontium-88. They measure the static nonlinear response and invert it. Feed-forward correction widens the linear range. Spurious tones drop by three to five decibels. Bell-state tests confirm better gate fidelity.
arxiv-2603-27961: Yasmeen, Ram, and Kundu present a radar sensing setup built on a 1-bit quantized reconfigurable intelligent surface. The surface steers electromagnetic waves in set patterns, which helps radar see targets in shadowed or off-axis spots. The team derives formulas for the scattered field and radar cross section, then checks them against full-wave simulations. A built surface run at 5.5 GHz matched the theory and recovered micro-Doppler signals that normal radar missed.
arxiv-2603-28061: Arora and three co-authors study how to test whether a real-valued function has a sparse form, using only a few queries. They cover three forms: functions that depend on few variables, sparse polynomials, and k-linear maps. Distance is measured under Gaussian samples with the L1 metric. For each form, the team gives an efficient tester and proves lower bounds that grow with k. The work extends property testing from discrete settings to the reals.
arxiv-2603-28161: Cai derives boundary four-point connection formulas for conformal loop ensembles with parameter between 4 and 8. These functions give the chance that boundary points link up through the random loops. For two special values, the formulas confirm exact results that Gori and Viti had guessed for critical percolation and the FK-Ising model. The FK-Ising case shows a logarithmic singularity. The method also covers mixed bulk and boundary connections, widening an older factorization result.
arxiv-2603-28261: Pannitto and six co-authors write guidelines for marking up sentences that speakers build together in conversation. In spoken data, one person may finish another's phrase, answer a question, or add a backchannel sound. Working in the Universal Dependencies framework, they propose two views: one split by speaker turns, one with links that cross turns. They also sharpen the line between reformulations and repairs. First annotation results show the scheme in action.
arxiv-2603-28661: Sangalli, Terazzi, and Zanotti revisit well-posedness for the linear acoustic wave equation. They ask whether classic well-posedness gives an isomorphism between chosen solution and data spaces. The answer matters for numerical method design. With an eigenfunction expansion, they reduce the equation to a system of ODEs. Standard Bochner space choices, they argue, clash with such a map because of resonant waves. A resonance-aware norm on the data space restores the isomorphism for each equation. A final section extends the results to other time dependent linear equations.
arxiv-2603-28761: Chen and co-authors revisit the S8 tension using cosmic shear in effective field theory at two-loop order. Cosmic shear probes distances, matter abundance, and clustering in the low-redshift universe. Baryonic effects usually force analysts to cut many usable scales. They show that the remaining scales are largely perturbative and fit two-loop predictions well. Their DES Year 3 analysis gives S8 near 0.783, or 0.802 with baryon acoustic data. In a dynamical dark energy model, they find no S8 tension in the growth of structure.
arxiv-2603-28861: Gajic studies charged scalar fields on near-extremal Reissner-Nordström black holes at late times. This is the second part of a series based on energy estimates. Gajic uses physical space methods to find the late time form of solutions. The fields form oscillating tails that decay by inverse power laws. The work gives the first pointwise decay bounds with no small charge assumption. It also proves growing instabilities in the radiation field at null infinity. In the extremal case, the same growth appears at the event horizon.
arxiv-2603-29061: Elmegreen and Hunter study star formation in dwarf irregular galaxies through cavity-ring structures. Unsharp-mask images of HI emission from 36 such galaxies show star formation in dispersed clouds and on cavity rims. The cavities are large, often circular or slightly sheared. Cloud peaks and ultraviolet star formation rates suggest a gas consumption time of about 3.2 billion years. Scale height estimates near 400 parsecs imply an efficiency per free fall time of about 1 percent. Cavity ages range from ten million to a hundred million years.
arxiv-2603-29661: Keith-Norambuena and co-authors add agenda steering to narrative extraction from document sets. Older methods trade off coherence, interaction, and multi-story support. Their method guides a pathfinding tool with a language model. At each step, the model ranks candidate documents by fit to a user's agenda. The storyline bends toward that agenda while coherence is guarded. Other agendas yield other storylines through the same corpus. Judges rated agenda fit higher than with keyword matching. The coherence cost stayed small in their tests.
arxiv-2603-29861: Schüßler and Prange score sentence-level readability in German ESG reports. Such reports must serve lay readers, not just finance experts. They extend an existing dataset with crowdsourced readability judgments. Native speakers mostly rate the sentences as easy, though ratings vary by person. The team compares classic formulas, LLM prompting, and a small tuned transformer. The tuned transformer predicts human ratings with the lowest error. Averaging several models helps slightly but runs slower.
arxiv-2604-00161: Longwei Xu and nine colleagues introduce TextAnchor-Bench, a benchmark testing whether vision-language models can ground queried text to the right image region. General and OCR-focused models still struggle to build accurate, stable text anchors. Their Q-Mask framework uses a causal query-driven mask decoder that makes visual masks step by step before OCR output, separating where text sits from what it says. Training on TextAnchor-26M image-text pairs with fine-grained masks, Q-Mask gains substantially in text anchoring and understanding across varied scenes.
arxiv-2604-00461: Kazemi and Behdinan review bipolar plates for proton exchange membrane fuel cells, a clean-energy path that runs on high-purity green hydrogen. In these cells, the bipolar plate largely sets efficiency, lifespan, and cost, through its material and its embedded flow channels. Standard manufacturing handles ordinary plate designs but fails on intricate, unconventional channel shapes, lacking the resolution for fine features and leaning on multi-step post-processing. The review surveys the newest processing methods for those unconventional channels.
arxiv-2604-00761: Samar Ansari introduces PrivHAR-Bench, a benchmark for judging privacy-preserving video action recognition across a graduated scale of privacy, not just clear versus altered video. Its 1,932 source videos span 9 tiers from light spatial blurring to cryptographic block scrambling, with background-removed versions and pose data included. Validation with R3D-18 shows accuracy falling from 88.8 percent on clear video. Encrypted, background-removed video scores far lower, mapping the privacy-utility trade-off.
arxiv-2604-00961: Dai and colleagues propose a Bayesian multi-group functional factor model for curves observed across different subject groups, such as trajectories over time, space, or wavelength. The model splits data into group-specific mean functions and latent components capturing common and distinct structures, represented with shared B-spline bases. A parameter-expanded cumulative shrinkage prior on factor loadings increases shrinkage and auto-selects the number of active factors. Tests on EEG data from alcoholic and healthy subjects reveal shared factors plus group-specific neural patterns.
arxiv-2604-01161: Rodionov, Garipov and Yakushev test reasoning models in three settings: problems padded with off-topic context, multi-turn chats with split tasks, and problems tucked inside complex tasks as subtasks. They find reasoning traces shrink by up to 74% for the same problem in varied context versus alone. Closer study links the shrinkage to drops in self-checking and doubt handling, such as double-checking. Even forced extra self-checks help only based on trace content and extra context, showing fragile reasoning toughness and context handling for language models.
arxiv-2604-01261: Ao, Tan, and Chen propose DySCo, a dynamic semantic compression framework for long-term time series forecasting. Longer lookback windows should add context, but in practice they add noise and redundant compute that hide long-term patterns. An entropy-guided sampling step keeps high-entropy segments and compresses redundant trends, while a hierarchical frequency-enhanced decomposition separates fast anomalies from slow patterns. A cross-scale mixer then fuses global context with local detail, boosting mainstream models at lower compute cost.
arxiv-2604-01461: Xie and colleagues present Peer Context Outlier Detection, which uses links between texts to improve scores in research literature. Methods such as prompt engineering and chain-of-thought focus on texts and ignore links across a corpus. Papers with similar experiment settings should draw similar conclusions, so the method compares extracted data to peer information. It adjusts confidence scores and flags low-confidence results for review. Experiments show up to 98 percent precision in outlier detection across 6 research domains, letting researchers focus on ambiguous cases.
arxiv-2604-01661: Stummer offers seven ontology-aware patterns in Gang-of-Four pattern language for clinical AI systems hardy against ontology drift. Clinical AI systems train on health data skewed by records, billing payoffs, and terminology splits. The patterns are Ontological Checkpoint, Dormancy-Aware Pipeline, Drift Sentinel, Dual-Ontology Layer, Reification Circuit Breaker, Terminology Version Gate, and Regulatory Compliance Adapter. They cover intake checks, rare signals, drift watch, dual records, feedback breaks, term versions, and rule checks. This paper reports no lab validation.
arxiv-2604-01961: Weihs and Schaeffer supply statistical guarantees for learning families of operators from hierarchical data. Samples arrive in tiers: operator instances, then input functions, then evaluation points, all noisy. For separable models built on the Multiple Neural Operator design, they derive metric entropy bounds for deep ReLU combinations and combine them with approximation results. The result is an explicit trade off between approximation and estimation error, with a clear learning rate in the operator sampling budget.
arxiv-2604-02261: Tan and colleagues report a peculiar magnetar X ray burst from SGR J1935+2154, caught by GECAM and linked to a fast radio burst. Dubbed MXB 221120, its light curve fits a single fast rise exponential decay shape overlaid with narrow pulses, plus a possible oscillation near 18 Hz. Its spectrum is thermal, the first thermal spectrum among fast radio burst linked bursts from this magnetar. Longer and hotter than single episode peers, it stands out as an outlier, hinting at an extreme production mechanism.
arxiv-2604-02361: Suzuki and colleagues detect internet route changes from traceroute latency alone with TRACE. Rolling statistics and context patterns capture time patterns, feeding a stacked ensemble of gradient boosted decision trees tuned by a meta learner. Thresholds set for the rarity of routing events handle class imbalance. The pipeline beats traditional baselines on route change detection, offering a control plane independent view of routing instability from endpoint measurements only.
arxiv-2604-02761: Kumari and Deb present the first systematic sustainability study of prompt strategies for small-language-model test generation. Seven prompt strategies across three open-source models are judged jointly on time, token use, energy, carbon, and coverage quality. Prompt choice has a large independent effect on sustainability, often outweighing model choice itself, with reasoning-heavy strategies costing far more than leaner ones for similar coverage.
arxiv-2604-03261: Kang, Noels, and De Bie present VIGIL, the first browser extension that spots and softens cognitive-bias triggers in online text as users scroll. It offers LLM-powered rewording that can be fully undone, plus privacy tiers from fully offline to cloud, and it accepts third-party plugins. The tool is open source, with several plugins already validated against language benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-03461: Alisic and Amin extend sensor-spoofing analysis from linear state spaces to Lie groups, where noncommutative dynamics can distort attacks. They prove a transferable attack must commute with the system flow, isolating such attacks to an invariant subspace. Small deviations reveal an asymmetry: the flow's adjoint action distorts the impact of non-commuting parts, and turning maneuvers on a Dubins unicycle shrink the transferable subspace to one direction.
arxiv-2604-03561: Ma, Ye, and Xiao introduce AdWise, a tool that joins static ad analysis and live UI search with large language models to detect mobile ads and assist rule checks. AdWise first finds UI widgets used to place ads. It then guides live search with window-graph, meaning-based, and layout guidance from static analysis and placement habits. On 100 benchmark apps, AdWise beats the strongest baseline by about 26 points in ad-widget finding. It finds 34.34 percent more breaches across six breach types.
arxiv-2604-03661: The SHiP Collaboration measured muon pairs from 400 GeV/c protons striking a thick molybdenum and tungsten target at CERN, a replica of the planned SHiP target. The data showed clear J/psi production, though at a lower rate than simulation predicted, which eases the job of the planned muon shield. The measured cross-section per nucleon came to 1.18 nanobarns, close to an earlier NA50 value within errors.
arxiv-2604-03761: Barış Bayraktar and colleagues re-placed the dwarf galaxy PEARLSDG, once thought an exotic isolated quiescent dwarf, inside a galaxy group at about 124 megaparsecs, far beyond the earlier 30. Fitting its light with parametric and nonparametric star-formation histories, they found a metallicity and mass that sit on the standard relation. Its quiet history now reads as environmental quenching, not oddity.
arxiv-2604-03961: Li Lin offered Financial Relativity, a shape-based view of asset pricing that drops the ranking between real-world and risk-neutral measures. Final facts shape odds geometry, which in turn governs how facts show up in prices. Prices become shape shadows of final payoffs onto information spaces, with volatility arising from after-the-fact doubt. The view unifies price swings, event-driven moves, and risk premia, and yields testable links between price swings and after-the-fact variance.
arxiv-2604-04161: Yuanchang Liang and team proposed Adaptive Action Chunking, a strategy that varies action-chunk size at inference time for vision-language-action robot models. Fixed chunk lengths blunt responsiveness when large and cause jerky mode-jumping when small. Their method uses action entropy as the cue to size each chunk from current predictions. Tests across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks showed substantial gains over state-of-the-art alternatives.
arxiv-2604-04261: Srewa, Zhao and Elmalaki tackle fair alignment when many groups with different values share one language model. In federated learning from human feedback, groups share a policy without pooling preference data, so fair reward merging matters. Averaging shortchanges the worst-served groups, while taking the minimum lifts them at the cost of overall alignment. Their APPA framework reweights group rewards from past alignment scores, favouring lagging groups without harming strong ones. Tests show worst-group alignment up by 28 percent over averaging, with overall alignment above the minimum approach.
arxiv-2604-04361: Cao and colleagues evaluate three ways to make simulated pupils feel authentic for mathematics teacher training. Zero- or few-shot prompting often yields fake knowledge and language. Fine-tuning, multi-agent setups and Direct Preference Optimization all improve cognitive and linguistic authenticity over few-shot prompts. Interviews with eight pre-service teachers and researchers show distinct trade-offs. The fine-tuned model gives realistic, brief replies but fewer chances to stretch pupil thinking, while multi-agent and DPO versions spell out pupil reasoning. The paper weighs authenticity against instructional value.
arxiv-2604-04561: Mouzouni maps what makes language-model agents with tool access exploit vulnerabilities. Within planted test-runner vulnerabilities, nine of twelve dimensions produce no detectable exploitation at 50 trials per cell. But goal reframing reliably triggers exploitation. A puzzle-solving framing produces 38 to 40 percent exploitation on Claude Sonnet 4 despite the rule instruction, replicating across four models. Agents do not override the rules; they reinterpret the task so that exploitative actions become task-aligned. GPT-4.1 shows no exploitation across 1,850 trials, and newer OpenAI models look safer over time, though capability differences confound.
arxiv-2604-04961: Vallarino studies identification in nonlinear dynamic systems on unknown interaction networks. The system evolves through an unseen link matrix that spreads shocks via a nonlinear operator. He shows the network cannot be found in general, since finding it needs varied spectral patterns. It can be found when the network creates distinct covariance patterns through uneven boosting of modes. When the spectrum narrows, the network mimics common shocks, and it cannot be found.
arxiv-2604-05161: Marković and three colleagues define SMB algebras: semilattices in which each element is blown up into a Mal'cev algebra. They publish old proofs that some SMB algebras induce tractable Constraint Satisfaction templates. They then reprove that all SMB algebras induce tractable Constraint Satisfaction templates, a result already proved by Bulatov. They also compare the two general CSP Dichotomy proofs, showing they are more similar than initially thought for SMB algebras. The paper is the second in a series on SMB algebras and a precursor to work on Dichotomy proof similarities.
arxiv-2604-05361: Cen, Ou, and Vong offer a symmetric fractional-order reduction method for fractional wave equations on uneven time grids, where solutions lack smoothness. They pick best parameter values for L-type schemes on such grids, adapting tools made for diffusion-wave problems. Tests with numbers back the new algorithms as fast and exact.
arxiv-2604-05461: He, Tang, and Chen help post authors escape information cocoons, where stance-aware ranking shows posts mainly to like-minded readers. Their ContentFuzz tool guides a language model to rewrite posts with feedback from stance detectors, keeping human-read meaning while flipping machine-assigned stance labels. Tests across four detectors, three datasets, and two languages show labels shift while meaning holds.
arxiv-2604-05561: Xu and eight colleagues sharpen the standard galaxy-halo link, subhalo abundance matching, which misses observed clustering in detail. Their CS-SHAM plan matches central and satellite galaxies apart and adds three knobs for the satellite share. Mock tests recover clustering and halo occupation well, showing clustering pins down big halos best.
arxiv-2604-05661: Jabal Ameli, Nederlof, and Wang improve space-time tradeoffs for permutation problems over additively idempotent semirings. Their traveling salesman algorithm reaches a time-space product at most 3.1861 to the power N, beating the prior bound and breaking a barrier shown optimal in the old framework. A new chain-efficiency parameter for set systems drives the gain and disproves a Johnson-Leader-Russell conjecture.
arxiv-2604-06061: Buchnick and three colleagues' 2026 paper presents PromptEvolver, a method for recovering a text prompt that rebuilds a given image faithfully. Finding such prompts by trial and error is slow, and current inversion methods often return poor rebuilds with unnatural, hard-to-read prompts. PromptEvolver instead evolves natural-language prompts with a genetic algorithm, guided by a strong vision-language model. It needs only image outputs, so it works on black-box generators. Across several inversion benchmarks, it consistently beats competing methods.
arxiv-2604-06361: Crisman, Quartin, and Rebouças combine supernova peculiar velocities, which trace large-scale structure, with CMB data to measure curvature and growth. Pantheon+, Dark Energy Survey, and Planck data measure wobble, growth, and curvature at once. Pantheon+ supernovae alone give wobble near three-quarters. Free growth and curvature hint at positive curvature near minus 0.011, ruling out flatness for Pantheon+ with CMB data. Growth near one-half matches relativity. Tangle among curvature, growth, and Hubble constant broadens the spread; SH0ES data recast tension as negative curvature and low growth.
arxiv-2604-06561: Ho and three colleagues speed 4D spectral imaging with a neural model. Spectral imaging reveals rapid dynamics, but mapping space-varying couplings in 2D IR spectra demands overly long capture. It reconstructs dense IR images from sparse data. A net maps sub-sampled points to levels. Results faithfully recover wavy and non-wavy motion. Loss-aware sampling adds informative samples during tests. The approach recovers high-fidelity spectra on one-thirty-second of the budget, cutting time up to 32-fold. The framework scales to hypercube-data experiments.
arxiv-2604-07061: Baggioli, Falk, and Kob review how flaw ideas from crystals might help explain glasses and other solids with no neat grid. In crystals, flaws in the grid shape how a solid breaks, moves ions, and melts in thin sheets, but glasses lack a neat grid to pin such flaws to. Recent work shows that signs tied to flaws still turn up in disordered solids, hinting the same ideas may guide their strength and shifting motion. The paper pulls together theory, computer runs, and lab work, and closes with open puzzles.
arxiv-2604-07161: Benbrik and five colleagues examine what happens when heavy vector-like bottom quarks join a two-Higgs-doublet model, a theory with an extra Higgs family. The new quarks open decay routes that collider searches focused on ordinary final states usually miss, and those routes weaken the current mass limits. A lone new quark drops from about 1.5 to 1.34 trillion electron volts, while doublet versions relax further to near 0.98, driven by decays into Higgs bosons.
arxiv-2604-07361: Dong and four colleagues present BLEG, a way to boost graph neural nets for brain-network analysis with a large language model. Graph nets on fMRI data suffer from sparse features and thin domain knowledge in single-modality graphs. BLEG asks the language model for augmented texts, tunes a language model cheaply for richer text features, aligns those features with graph features in training, and tunes an adapter per task. Tests across datasets show BLEG beats prior methods, and a loss aligning language and graph outputs lifts results further.
arxiv-2604-07461: Rugheimer and colleagues ask how well the LIFE interferometer concept could spot water vapor, a proxy for oceans, on Earth-like exoplanets. They model an Earth-like atmosphere across water pressures from very low to one bar, simulating LIFE noise and running Bayesian retrievals under three vertical water profiles. Detectability hinges on the assumed profile: saturated features blind LIFE to the wettest cases, and no profile yields a detection at the lowest pressures. For an Earth-like profile, LIFE constrains water from about a thousandth up to one bar.
arxiv-2604-07761: Gundavarapu, Dhas, and Roy find a Kapitza-style surface instability in a falling film that needs no inertia. The trick is viscosity that varies steadily across the film thickness. Long-wave analysis and Chebyshev spectral computation solve the coupled perturbation problem. The instability appears only inside a finite window of Péclet numbers, which compare flow with diffusion. Stronger stratification lowers the critical Péclet number, widens the unstable wavenumber range, and speeds growth, as vorticity lags behind interface displacement.
arxiv-2604-08761: Cheng, Jin, and Zhang tackle sign language reading at vocabulary scale with PHONSSM, a state space model built on phonological structure. Older models treat signs as atomic patterns and collapse at realistic sizes, but PHONSSM decomposes signs into handshape, location, movement, and orientation through graph attention, factorized subspaces, and prototypical classification. On 5,565 American Sign Language signs from skeleton data alone, it reaches 72.1 percent on WLASL2000 and transfers zero shot to ASL Citizen.
arxiv-2604-08861: Deng and four colleagues propose crosstalk robust super two qubit shape gates using tunable couplers. Coupler based gates ease layout and ease rate crowding, but cutting crosstalk while speeding gate time remains an open tradeoff. Adding tunable degrees of freedom steers motion along desired paths, freely dodging crosstalk touchy regions. Tests show strong crosstalk cut with fast gates and strong toughness to qubit rate drift. High faithfulness holds even with high rate wobble terms and decay, a feasible path to robust fast two qubit gates.
arxiv-2604-09461: dos Santos studies Wakimoto-type free field builds for superelliptic affine Lie algebras, focused on sl-2. Clear operators are built from m ghost Fock spaces combined by tensor product. They recover standard Wakimoto product rules in the even sector and correct charge links in the odd sector. The author then proves leftover mixed-sector brackets are blocked by two separate mechanisms. One is a charge-residue block from Kähler differential recurrence, and the other is a Heisenberg branch-cut block from non-integer exponents, yielding an obstruction theorem.
arxiv-2604-09561: Calin presents the first study of social structure among self-governing AI agents on a live network. He examines 626 agents, mostly OpenClaw instances that found and joined the Pilot Protocol on their own. Since message contents are fully encrypted, he works from metadata alone: trust links, capability tags, and registry patterns. The trust network looks strikingly human, with small-world structure, Dunbar-like layers, and preferential attachment, yet 64 percent of agents also trust themselves, and a large fringe stays unintegrated.
arxiv-2604-09961: Leißa and Griebler replace rule with free names for single-naming builders, arguing rule is loose for modern higher-order code. Control flow blurs data flow, and rule needs first-order control-flow graphs. Higher-order programs without an open graph break the ruled-use rule. Phi-functions and inputs plainly express data ties, letting rule-built tests with better care. A lean method maintains free-variable sets in mutable form, and a nesting tree from variable ties supports shaped tests. Benchmarks show log-linear scaling with program size.
arxiv-2604-10361: Angel offers a scheme for deformation theory and multi-param lasting. Multi-param lasting modules have wild form type, blocking sorting and clarity. An idea guide bridges shape data study and bend theory, reading shakes as bends and calm as smooth moduli spaces. Sums of link groups for small-poset modules range from stiffness to large bend clans. Block classes vanish on posets but prove sure on larger grids, marking a deep moduli shift. A guess relates weaving distance to derived folding through two-way match.
arxiv-2604-10561: Long and Luo pin down aluminum's liquid vapor critical point at last. Past guesses for the critical temperature sprawled across nearly 4,000 kelvin. Deep potential runs trained on electronic structure data test several density functionals, with PBEsol best. Spinodal plus coexistence runs converge on 6,531 to 6,576 kelvin and 1.6 kbar. The density lands near two thirds of a gram per cubic centimetre, with errors near 50 kelvin.
arxiv-2604-10861: Dou and colleagues offer electronic and photonic stochastic neurons for physical nets, where learning and inference run. The electronic neuron tunnels electrons through a quantum dot, with dot charge as its base. The photonic neuron uses a photon source driving one of two modes linked by a tunable link, with idle occupation as its base. Training tests MNIST sorting with hidden-layer nets, using stochastic neurons and coherently-driven detector neurons. Using real outputs in the backward pass, the net tops 97 percent in trials, and holds under noise and doubt.
arxiv-2604-11061: Zhong and four colleagues introduce Pando, a benchmark for interpretability when models will not explain themselves. Many evaluations ignore whether black-box prompting recovers target behaviour. White-box gains may then reflect elicitation, not internal signal. Pando uses an axis: models give faithful, no, or unfaithful explanations of a distractor rule. Across 720 models with hidden rules, agents predict held-out decisions from pairs plus one output. Faithful explanations let black-box elicitation match white-box methods. With absent or misleading explanations, gradient attribution improves scores by several points.
arxiv-2604-11261: Binkyte and five colleagues propose treating AI interactions as research objects to govern generative AI in science. Rather than debating whether AI is author or tool, their AI-RO framework logs model settings, prompts, and outputs as inspectable, accountable parts of the workflow. It draws on Research Object theory and FAIR principles. A demo writing pipeline synthesizes human-written literature notes under explicit constraints and produces a verifiable provenance record, with special attention to security and privacy research.
arxiv-2604-11861: Kedia, Makam, Hamann, and Sundaram present BIND-USBL, a joint scheme that bounds drift for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) using surface vessels. With no GPS under water, AUVs rely on inertial dead reckoning, which drifts without bound. Surface vessels with acoustic ultra-short-baseline positioning send fixes now and then, and the scheme links survey scale and anchor spots to coverage, plans shared-channel uplinks, and fuses late fixes with dead reckoning. Test runs show coverage, team makeup, and formation shape jointly set performance.
arxiv-2604-13161: Romare, Shaffer, Levchenko, Huang, and Esterlis compute the superconducting transition temperature of the 2D attractive Hubbard model near ordinary and higher-order Van Hove singularities using determinant quantum Monte Carlo. For couplings up to about a third of the bandwidth, transition temperature rises near the Van Hove point, though less than weak-coupling theory expects. Sharpening the singularity adds only a small further rise. At stronger couplings the peak shifts away from the Van Hove point to an unrelated density, with the maximum reached at intermediate coupling strength.
arxiv-2604-13261: Akella and Iizuka study replica symmetry breaking for multi-entropy in random tensor network domain-wall spin models. Their main result blocks symmetry breaking for all indices and part counts. Edge permutations for multi-entropy run along incompatible axis directions of the replica hypercube, with no nontrivial geodesic middle step. Entanglement negativity, by contrast, admits such an aided saddle and does show symmetry breaking. A toy Z2 gauge add-on agrees: multi-entropy shows no symmetry breaking at indices 2 and 3 while negativity keeps showing it.
arxiv-2604-13461: Vakhnovskyi proposes a cascading control architecture that makes vapour pressure deficit the primary outer-loop variable for indoor farming climate control. Conventional independent PID loops for temperature and humidity fight each other through cross-coupling, wasting 20 to 40 percent of HVAC energy. A 7-3-3 neural network optimizer picks energy-minimal temperature-humidity setpoints along the deficit constraint surface, feeding inner PID loops that run HVAC actuators, with Lyapunov analysis guaranteeing bounded gains. Deployment across more than 30 facilities over seven years cuts HVAC energy by 30 to 38 percent and improves deficit stability markedly.
arxiv-2604-13861: Ganesh optimizes T20 batting orders and bowling plans with a Markov Decision Process framework, scoring by win and defend chances rather than expected runs. A three-phase profile engine for Powerplay, Middle, and Death uses James-Stein shrinkage, blending sparse phase statistics toward league averages. Profiles come from 1,161 IPL records from 2008 to 2025, with probabilities from Monte Carlo simulation over 50,000 innings. In two 2026 IPL matches, the Mumbai Indians order lifts win probability by 4.1 percentage points, and the Gujarat Titans plan lifts defend probability by 5.2 points.
arxiv-2604-13961: Boni and colleagues trim Tiny U-Net for drone-based oil-spill monitoring, where full inference wastes effort on easy radar images. An early-exit branch returns a prediction once a confidence score passes a tunable threshold, skipping deeper layers. The design matches full-model IoU of 0.79 while cutting multiplications by up to 42 percent at an aggressive threshold, saving dynamic power.
arxiv-2604-14061: Liu studies the largest average inner product of a random vector with a standard normal vector. The vectors pair under a mutual-information constraint or penalty. He shows this maximum equals a truncated rate-distortion integral, up to universal constants. The proof lifts the problem to a Gaussian process. That process runs over a random subset of a type class. A form of the majorizing measure theorem then finishes the argument.
arxiv-2604-14161: Varga tests whether large language models can spot methodological flaws in published work, using a gesture-recognition paper for drone rescue that reports near-perfect accuracy on a small human dataset. He first argues the evaluation protocol matches subject-level leakage from non-independent training and test splits. Six leading models, each reading the paper cold under an identical prompt, all flag the evaluation as flawed and blame the split. That agreement suggests such models could aid reproducibility checks and scientific auditing.
arxiv-2604-14261: Li and nine colleagues argue that LLM peer reviewers fail by skipping two human habits: explicit rubrics and grounding in existing work. Their REVIEWBENCH benchmark grades review text against paper-specific rubrics drawn from official guidelines, paper content, and human reviews. Their REVIEWGROUNDER framework splits reviewing into drafting and grounding stages, enriching thin drafts with targeted evidence. On REVIEWBENCH it beats stronger and larger backbones, including GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek-R1-670B, on human alignment and rubric-based quality across eight dimensions.
arxiv-2604-14661: Su, Wu, Huang, and Feng present AIPC, an agent-driven approach automating edge AI model deployment in constrained, verifiable stages. Deployment spans conversion, compatibility, calibration, integration, and validation, a long failure-prone workflow demanding scarce expertise. AIPC injects deployment knowledge into how agents act, through Agent Skills, helper scripts, and stage-wise validation, cutting expertise and time needs.
